items.headline: Lord Krishna's message is timeless, says MLA
items.gist: Mangaluru South MLA D Vedavyas Kamath said Lord Sri Krishna's teachings remain relevant to all sections of society while inaugurating Sri Krishna Janmashtami celebrations at Kudmul Ranga Rao Town Hall organised by the Dakshina Kannada district administration, DK Zilla Panchayat and the Department of Kannada and Culture. MUDA Chairman Santosh Kumar Shetty, Kannada Sahitya Parishat President Srinath, Additional SP Anil Kumar Bhoomireddy and other officials attended the event.

items.headline: Raaga Sudha, an evening dedicated to Hindustani classical music
items.gist: Kala Sadhana, in association with the Ramakrishna Mission, is organising 'Raaga Sudha', an evening of Hindustani classical music at Sri Ramakrishna Mutt near Sri Mangaladevi Temple in Mangaluru on September 6 at 5 pm. items.headline: Youngest record holder
items.gist: Joash, aged 7 years and 2 months and the grandson of retired principal Antony A J and Dr Beena of Mangaluru, entered the India Book of Records by identifying 185 breeds of dogs on a laptop screen in 6 minutes and 26 seconds. His parents are Sheetal and Dr Ajoy.

items.headline: Worm allegedly found inside egg: Blinkit facility sealed
items.gist: Food safety officials inspected a Blinkit online retail facility in Mangaluru after a customer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform, with the complaint reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader. During inspection of the facility at Falnir Square in Falnir, officials found packets containing broken eggs and directed staff to remove and dispose of affected stock; the storage room was temporarily closed and sealed for cleaning and sanitisation, and the Food Safety Department said it would issue a notice seeking an explanation.

items.headline: 16-coach Vande Bharat to undergo Yeshwanthpur–Mangaluru test run
items.gist: A 16-coach Vande Bharat Express will undertake a trial run between Yeshwanthpur and Mangaluru Central on Saturday, September 5, as directed by the Railway Board. The train will leave Yeshwanthpur at 6.05am and arrive at Mangaluru Central at 2.25pm, halting at Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road and Padil; it returns from Mangaluru Central at 3pm and reaches Yeshwanthpur at 11pm.
items.paragraph: A 16-coach Vande Bharat Express will undertake a trial run between Yeshwanthpur and Mangaluru Central on Saturday, September 5, as directed by the Railway Board. The train will leave Yeshwanthpur at 6.05am and arrive at Mangaluru Central at 2.25pm, halting at Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road and Padil; it returns from Mangaluru Central at 3pm and reaches Yeshwanthpur at 11pm. The trial assumes importance as the route includes the challenging ghat section, where officials will assess operational performance under varying gradients and explore reducing the proposed journey time of more than eight hours without compromising safety.

items.headline: 3 booked for 'abusing, threatening' students
items.gist: Three persons have been booked for allegedly abusing and threatening four private college students at a cafe near Mangaluru on September 3, police said on Friday. The accused — Rithil Poojary, Prem Bhandari and Sanjay Hegde — allegedly entered the cafe near the Moodbidri bus stand without permission and questioned the students; two of the accused are alleged to be Sangh Parivar activists.
items.paragraph: Three persons have been booked for allegedly abusing and threatening four private college students at a cafe near Mangaluru on September 3, police said on Friday. The accused — Rithil Poojary, Prem Bhandari and Sanjay Hegde — allegedly entered the cafe near the Moodbidri bus stand without permission and questioned the students; two of the accused are alleged to be Sangh Parivar activists. Police Sub-Inspector Pratibha filed a complaint and registered a case under Sections 126(2), 352, 351(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; Bhandari and Hegde had previously figured in four cases at Moodbidri police station and a rowdy sheet has reportedly been opened against them.

items.headline: FIR against NITK professors over alleged NCC TA/DA fraud
items.gist: Surathkal Police have registered an FIR against two NITK Surathkal professors — Associate NCC Officers Prof P Johnson and Prof H Shivananda — over alleged fraud in NCC TA/DA claim bills based on false documents, according to Deccan Herald. Police have detained the duo and an internal investigation is underway at NITK, where the "2 Kar Engr Coy NCC (Army Wing)" unit has functioned since 1963 with around 160 enrolled students; NITK Director B Ravi said the unit should follow honesty and integrity, and Dr Mohan Lal Meena has been appointed NCC caretaker officer in place of the ANOs.

items.headline: Traffic curbs planned in Moodbidri to ease congestion
items.gist: Authorities have decided to introduce measures to ease traffic congestion in Moodbidri town, including restricting heavy vehicles between 7am and 9pm and issuing MDB identification marks and numbers for autorickshaws operating within the city. Lorries and other heavy vehicles will be diverted through the ring road and outer roads; signboards indicating one-way traffic and no-entry zones will be installed, private buses directed to enter the designated bus stand and adhere to permitted timings, and measures taken to curb overspeeding and inspect horns fitted on vehicles.

The decision followed a meeting attended by ACP Srikanth, municipal chief officer Indu M., inspector Rajendra, transport association representatives and others.

items.headline: NIT-K introduces revised 'bold and balanced' engineering curriculum
items.gist: The National Institute of Technology-Karnataka (NIT-K), Surathkal, said on Friday that it has introduced a revised, "bold and balanced" engineering curriculum for the BTech batch of 2026, reducing total credits while allowing Honours or Minors programmes. Credits from theory classes will now nearly equal those from practical activities outside the classroom, meaning students will effectively spend two-thirds of their time outside classrooms on laboratory work, life-skills activities, industry internship, R&D project and business startup planning.
items.paragraph: The National Institute of Technology-Karnataka (NIT-K), Surathkal, said on Friday that it has introduced a revised, "bold and balanced" engineering curriculum for the BTech batch of 2026, reducing total credits while allowing Honours or Minors programmes. Credits from theory classes will now nearly equal those from practical activities outside the classroom, meaning students will effectively spend two-thirds of their time outside classrooms on laboratory work, life-skills activities, industry internship, R&D project and business startup planning. Director B. Ravi said the institute aims to prepare students for the AI era and produce well-rounded individuals contributing to Viksit Bharat by 2047.

items.headline: Temple town immerses in devotional fervour during Janmashtami celebrations
items.gist: Thousands of devotees gathered at Sri Krishna Mutt in Udupi as the sacred Arghya Pradana ritual marking Lord Krishna's birth was performed at 12:12 AM on September 5 at Seetha Mantap, led by Shiroor Mutt seer Sri Vedavardhana Theertha Swami. Car Street was decorated with 13 triangular wooden Gurjis and two large pavilions, with 47 earthen pots suspended for traditional Mosaru Kudike and Vittla Pindi celebrations scheduled for Saturday.

items.gist: Sri Vedavardhana Theertha Swami of Shiroor Mutt performed the Mahapuja at Krishna Mutt with the deity adorned in a special Yashoda Krishna Alankara, as the sanctum sanctorum and surrounding mantapas were decorated with chrysanthemums and marigolds. items.headline: Two chosen for best teacher award
items.gist: Two teachers from Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts have been selected for the State-level Best Teacher Award for 2026-27. Ashoka, a teacher at Government Higher Primary School, Kundapur taluk, Udupi district, is among 20 primary school teachers selected for the State award, while Roshan Alexander Pinto, Assistant Teacher, Grade II, Carmel High School, Bantwal taluk, Dakshina Kannada district, is among 11 high school teachers chosen.
items.paragraph: Two teachers from Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts have been selected for the State-level Best Teacher Award for 2026-27. Ashoka, a teacher at Government Higher Primary School, Kundapur taluk, Udupi district, is among 20 primary school teachers selected for the State award, while Roshan Alexander Pinto, Assistant Teacher, Grade II, Carmel High School, Bantwal taluk, Dakshina Kannada district, is among 11 high school teachers chosen. items.headline: No end to cyber fraud: ₹26 crore lost in two and a half years
items.gist: Despite sustained awareness campaigns, cyber fraud continues to pose a serious threat in Uttara Kannada, with fraudsters allegedly siphoning off nearly ₹26 crore from residents over the past two and a half years. According to the state Home Department, 237 cyber fraud cases were registered at the Uttara Kannada cyber police station during the period, 14 accused were arrested, and only around ₹1.85 crore could be recovered; fraudsters have used fake online job offers, stock market investment scams, impersonation of bank or government officials, KYC update requests and social media targeting.

items.headline: Tunnel may damage Lalbagh rock, warns GSI
items.gist: A Geological Survey of India expert committee has flagged serious geological, structural and groundwater risks to Lalbagh and its three-billion-year-old Lalbagh rock in a 27-page report submitted to the government in April. The committee warned that tunneling and excavation could damage the ancient rock mass, widen existing cracks and threaten the Kempegowda tower, and flagged proposed Shaft 4 adjacent to the National Geological Monument as a critical concern.

The committee warned that tunneling and excavation could damage the ancient rock mass, widen existing cracks and threaten the Kempegowda tower, and flagged proposed Shaft 4 adjacent to the National Geological Monument as a critical concern. The findings are significant as the state government was on the verge of awarding the Rs 22,267-crore, 16.75-km Hebbal–Central Silk Board tunnel road project to Adani Enterprises, the lowest bidder.

items.headline: Govt vehicles violate traffic rules, pile up over 82k cases in 3 years
items.gist: Karnataka government vehicles, including police and non-police department fleets, accumulated over 82,000 traffic violation cases between 2023 and July 2026 with Rs 19.56 crore in unpaid penalties, data presented in the Legislative Council showed. Authorities recovered only Rs 47.72 lakh, leaving over 97% unpaid, with Mysuru city recording 28,708 cases against non-police government vehicles in 2024; Home Minister Priyank Kharge said individual drivers, not the government exchequer, must pay the fines.

Das said he was 500 feet away when officials opened fire, escaped into the woods after being shot at and later admitted himself to a hospital, and claimed the group entered the forest for fishing, not poaching.

items.headline: K'taka SIR: Over 43.81L notices generated, 7.31L delivered
items.gist: Over 43.81 lakh notices have been generated in Karnataka's ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, of which 7.31 lakh have been delivered, the chief electoral officer's office said on Friday. The state has 4,46,38,124 electors as of September 4 — 2.21 crore male, 2.24 crore female and 2,871 transgender — with notices issued to electors in "no mapping" and "anomalies" categories; 36,49,371 notices remain pending delivery and 206 hearings have been completed since hearings began on September 3 and run until October 12.

items.headline: State turns to cloud seeding amid worsening drought
items.gist: Amid drought conditions, the Karnataka government on Friday launched a cloud-seeding programme at HAL airport, using a specially equipped light aircraft at an estimated cost of ₹28.52 crore. Water Resources Minister N.
items.paragraph: Amid drought conditions, the Karnataka government on Friday launched a cloud-seeding programme at HAL airport, using a specially equipped light aircraft at an estimated cost of ₹28.52 crore. Water Resources Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy said an earlier operation had a success rate of only 35%, but every effort to augment water availability mattered as the State had received little rainfall and the southwest monsoon would conclude by the end of this month, warning that without adequate drinking water stored by then scarcity could persist until next June. A technical advisory committee will update information every two hours and aircraft will be deployed to rainfall-deficit areas, reservoir catchments and distressed districts when suitable clouds are detected using Doppler radar.

items.headline: Crop loss study in 24 more taluks of 11 districts
items.gist: The state government ordered ground-truthing in 24 additional taluks across 11 districts including Dharwad, Vijayapura, Raichur, Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru, Shivamogga, Haveri, Bidar, Koppal and Tumakuru to assess drought severity following farmer protests, with a final report expected by September 11. Taluks may be declared moderately drought-affected if crop loss exceeds 33% or severely affected if loss exceeds 50%, after 101 taluks were already identified as drought-hit.

items.headline: Criminal cases will be filed against lake encroachers: Khandre
items.gist: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has warned that any encroachment of lakes belonging to and maintained by gram panchayats will be cleared and criminal cases filed against encroachers, saying Karnataka has 32,504 such lakes, of which 11,498 have been encroached upon, with encroachments cleared from 6,670 lakes but persisting in 4,828 lakes covering 11,671 acres. He said Karnataka is the second most drought-prone State with declining groundwater, that surface water sources must be protected, and that Karnataka is the first State to undertake water budgeting and has implemented continuous drinking water supply in 268 villages yielding a 7% saving.

items.headline: K'taka to collect DNA samples of kin of missing Nepal tourists
items.gist: The Karnataka government is collecting DNA samples from first-degree relatives of 26 people from the state, including 17 Bengalureans, who remain untraceable after the August 26 floods in Nepal, coordinating with the Ministry of External Affairs to match samples with mortal remains found there. Missing persons named include Hrishikesh HS, Reena Kathandaraman and Nallaipalli Ramakrishnan from Whitefield and 44-year-old S Kuzhanthaivelan.

items.headline: School ceiling collapse: Lokayukta cops register suo motu case
items.gist: Lokayukta police in Bagalkot registered a suo motu case after a student was injured when a concrete ceiling collapsed at a government higher primary school in Mugalolli Tanda, issuing notices to high-ranking officials in the Education and PWD departments. The Lokayukta directed inspection of other government school buildings and ordered a safety audit of all school buildings in the state.

items.headline: RSS march: KSAT stays suspension of two Yadgir teachers
items.gist: The Kalaburagi bench of the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal stayed the suspension of headmaster Anna Saheb and assistant teacher Gururaj Joshi from Yadgir, suspended by the DDPI for participating in an RSS Patha Sanchalana march in October last year. The tribunal held that participation in a programme by a non-political entity does not violate Karnataka Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 2021, and noted no official order prohibits officials from RSS events, staying the order until October 9.

items.headline: Industry participation crucial for PM-SETU scheme: Minister
items.gist: Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil on Friday urged public and private sector industries to participate in the PM-SETU scheme upgrading 48 Industrial Training Institutes under a hub-and-spoke model covering 12 hubs with four ITIs each. In Bengaluru Urban, Peenya ITI will serve as the hub with Tumakuru Road, Domlur, Hosur Road and Devanahalli as spokes; in Kalaburagi, the Government ITI for Boys will be the hub with Sedam, Afzalpur, Jewargi and the Government ITI for Women as spokes, with a Special Purpose Vehicle including six industry representatives and eligibility for companies with at least Rs 500 crore turnover and 1,000 employees.

items.headline: Nostalgia to return to screens
items.gist: Nagathihalli Chandrashekhar's 1997 Kannada film 'America America', the first Kannada film screened widely outside India and a National Award winner that ran over a year at Bengaluru's Abhinaya theatre, gets a sequel 'America America 2' releasing September 11. Adapted from Sahana Vijay Kumar's novel 'Kshame' rather than continuing the original love story, the sequel juxtaposes serene Mysuru against turbulent Seattle to examine whether women's economic independence over three decades has translated into happiness and how interpretations of love and relationships have changed.

items.headline: Asiad-bound athletes get a taste of Japan in Bengaluru
items.gist: SAI Bengaluru is acclimatising Asian Games-bound athletes including Karnataka pole vaulter G Sindhushree and Supriya B with Japanese cuisine such as sushi, unagi and uramaki, a simulator container room replicating compact Japan accommodation, and a pamphlet on greetings, transport, currency and etiquette. Chef V Jeyaraj's kitchen feeds around 350 athletes daily; regional director Vishnu Sudhakaran said the food programme began in January and expanded once the final squad was known in July ahead of Aichi-Nagoya from September 19 to October 4.

items.headline: KSCA President's XI scores thrilling win
items.gist: KSCA President's XI recorded an exciting one-wicket win over Goa CA in their Dr. (Capt.) K.
items.paragraph: KSCA President's XI recorded an exciting one-wicket win over Goa CA in their Dr. (Capt.) K. Thimappiah Memorial tournament match at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium here on Friday. Set a target of 150, KSCA President's XI fell to 100 for eight when Anvay Dravid (30) was dismissed, but tailenders Manvanth Kumar (18), Shikhar Shetty (28 n.o.) and Mohsin Khan (six n.o.) held firm to guide the side to a win; Goa CA made 338 and 207 while KSCA President's XI replied with 396 and 151/9 in 42.1 overs (Ruthvik Nai 5/32). At Alur, spinners Paras Gurbax Arya (four for 40) and Dheeraj Gowda (five for 19) powered KSCA Secretary's XI past Baroda CA, and at Mysuru left-arm spinner Saurabh Kumar (five for 80), supported by medium-pacer Madhav Rayudu (three for 43), enabled Andhra CA to register a 10-run win over Himachal Pradesh CA.

items.headline: SIR in K'taka: 43.81 lakh notice generated
items.gist: Over 43.81 lakh notices have been generated in Karnataka's ongoing SIR of electoral rolls, of which 7.31 lakh have been delivered to electors, the chief electoral officer's office said Friday. The State has 4,46,38,124 electors as of September 4 — 2.21 crore male, 2.24 crore female and 2,871 transgender — with notices issued to those in "no mapping" and "anomalies" categories; 43,81,141 of 43,81,143 planned notices have been generated, 36,49,371 remain pending delivery, and 206 hearings completed.

items.headline: Karnataka likely to revise government bus fares soon, says minister
items.gist: Transport Minister B. Suresh said the Karnataka government is preparing to revise state-run bus fares after refraining from increases despite rising fuel costs over eight months, with the four transport corporations suffering losses running into thousands of crores.
items.paragraph: Transport Minister B. Suresh said the Karnataka government is preparing to revise state-run bus fares after refraining from increases despite rising fuel costs over eight months, with the four transport corporations suffering losses running into thousands of crores. A committee headed by retired IAS officer Atul Tiwari is studying the issue and expected to submit its report shortly; the minister said any increase would be moderate given the drought situation. The government also plans free Shakti scheme smart cards for over one crore women at around ₹250 crore, BMTC procurement of 4,500 electric buses under PM E-DRIVE (3,800 twelve-metre and 900 nine-metre, about 400 air-conditioned) at roughly ₹600 crore annually, and a ₹2,000 crore Centre loan for new depots and upgraded bus stands.

items.headline: CoA awards on Sept 8
items.gist: Sir MV School of Architecture will host the Council of Architecture (CoA) National Awards for Excellence in Architectural Thesis for 2026 from September 8 to 10. This year's exhibits showcase projects on the revival of Art and Heritage of India, focusing on the Deccan region, and the event includes a closed jury of selected thesis projects from 100-plus institutions, a public heritage documentation exhibition, thesis presentations, and cultural and valedictory programmes.

items.headline: Three arrested for hunting two deer using electric wire
items.gist: Forest Department officials have arrested three persons — Banu, Shivu and Mahesh, residents of Nagavalli village and accused Nos. 2, 5 and 6 — for allegedly hunting two deer by electrifying a wire in the Sharavati Wildlife Sanctuary in Sagar taluk of Shivamogga district.
items.paragraph: Forest Department officials have arrested three persons — Banu, Shivu and Mahesh, residents of Nagavalli village and accused Nos. 2, 5 and 6 — for allegedly hunting two deer by electrifying a wire in the Sharavati Wildlife Sanctuary in Sagar taluk of Shivamogga district. The accused allegedly laid an electrified wire in farmland belonging to Shaji, electrocuted two male deer, butchered them for meat and buried skins and bones underground; three other accused — Shaji, Rama and Sridhar — are reportedly absconding, and officials are examining the source of electricity and whether similar offences occurred earlier.

items.gist: Uzbek chess prodigy Javokhir Sindarov said his preparations for the world championship match against defending champion D Gukesh will begin only after this month's Chess Olympiad, despite the Geneva showdown over 14 classical games from November 24 to December 12 between two 20-year-olds. items.headline: No time: Carlsen urges chess to look beyond him
items.gist: Five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen, speaking in Bengaluru ahead of the fourth Global Chess League where he will represent Alpine APL Pipers, said organisers should not shape chess's future around his preferences because his time at the top is "limited." Carlsen, who holds the highest rating in chess history at 2882 and leads the FIDE rankings, has opted out of the classical World Championship cycle but remains eager to compete in rapid formats like the GCL. He said new fans and formats over the last five to six years are interesting to be part of, but his motivation fluctuates tournament to tournament and the sport should innovate beyond what motivates him alone.

items.headline: Notification granting externment powers to SPs struck down by HC
items.gist: The High Court of Karnataka has struck down a notification issued on November 18, 2025 empowering Superintendents of Police in districts to pass externment orders under the Karnataka Police Act, 1963, holding that Section 55 empowers only the Police Commissioner in commissionerate cities, the District Magistrate elsewhere, and a specially empowered Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum observed the SP does not fall within categories contemplated by Section 55 and set aside an April 2026 externment order passed by the Belagavi SP against Chandrakant Shankar Vaddar, a 54-year-old labourer from Nippani, clarifying executive instructions cannot override express statutory provisions.

items.gist: Film director, actor and choreographer Prabhu Deva has been invited to inaugurate this year's Yuva Dasara in Mysuru. items.headline: Praja Seva meetings to be held at taluk, hobli levels on Saturdays
items.gist: The Praja Seva Abhiyan, to be launched across the State on Saturday through the Department of Prajaseva, aims to bring the administration to people's doorsteps every Saturday, with taluk and hobli meetings on the first and third Saturdays under the District In-charge Minister and on the second and fourth under the local MLA. The public will be informed at least 15 days in advance through pamphlets, pre-printed application forms and AI-based outbound calls; GramaOne kiosks will accept applications at venues, with separate queues for new grievances and for UPGRS cases unresolved or inadequately addressed after 21 days, and eligible beneficiaries may receive sanction or redressal letters on the spot.

items.headline: Complaints, applications received at meetings to be reviewed in three stages
items.gist: All applications and complaints received during the weekly Praja Seva Abhiyan will be systematically reviewed on Wednesdays in three stages: taluk-level review from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m.
items.paragraph: All applications and complaints received during the weekly Praja Seva Abhiyan will be systematically reviewed on Wednesdays in three stages: taluk-level review from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. by Tahsildars and Taluk Panchayat Executive Officers, sub-divisional review from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. by Assistant Commissioners, and district-level review from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. by Deputy Commissioners, with dissatisfied citizens able to appear in person at each stage. Applications not disposed of within the specified period will be automatically transferred to the head of the concerned department, a District In-charge Secretary will visit each district on the first and third Friday of every month, and progress will be reviewed by the Chief Secretary and Chief Minister.

items.headline: 32, including 7 women, rescued from bonded labour in sugarcane fields
items.gist: Thirty-two persons, including seven women, were rescued from alleged bonded labour at a sugarcane field in Ganganadoddi village in Chamarajanagar district on Tuesday following a tip-off from the Village Administrative Officer of Suleripalya Circle in Hanur taluk. Shanmugam has been identified as the main accused in an FIR registered at Ramapura police station; he allegedly brought 30 migrant labourers from Tamil Nadu and one each from Andhra Pradesh and Bihar, with associates Ruby, Ranjitha, Sarvanam and Karthik supervising and assaulting them.

items.headline: CM invites BJP leaders to join him in seeking farm loan waiver from Centre
items.gist: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday urged the Centre to waive farm loans in Karnataka in view of the drought and called upon BJP leaders to join him in pressing the demand in New Delhi, saying the State has declared 101 taluks as drought-affected for the kharif season following a deficit monsoon.
items.paragraph: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday urged the Centre to waive farm loans in Karnataka in view of the drought and called upon BJP leaders to join him in pressing the demand in New Delhi, saying the State has declared 101 taluks as drought-affected for the kharif season following a deficit monsoon. Speaking at Kudal Sangam in Bagalkot after a drought review, he reiterated Karnataka is facing one of the worst droughts in decades, pointed out BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra had demanded a farm loan waiver, and urged Mr. Vijayendra and Leader of Opposition R. Ashok to accompany him to Delhi; drought-hit taluks were listed as per Central calamity relief guidelines and the legislature will hold a special session from September 21 to 23 on the drought, agrarian crisis and the Kasturirangan report.

items.headline: Battle of the brains in Garden City
items.gist: The fourth edition of the Global Chess League — a joint venture of Tech Mahindra and FIDE — opens at the Lalit Ashok in Bengaluru on Saturday, bringing the world's leading chess players to the Garden City for the second time the league has been held in India after Season-3 in Mumbai; innovations such as no increment for the first 40 moves, four points for a win with black, mixed men's and women's teams, and a pre-match toss have drawn top players including Magnus Carlsen, whose Alpine Pipers are defending champions, and Viswanathan Anand, Alireza Firouzja, Javokhir Sindarov, Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Ian Nepomniachtchi.

items.headline: Assault on NEET protester's dad: Hindutva activist held
items.gist: Hindutva activist Swatantra Bhardwaj, who claimed he cracked the skull of protester Nishu Azad's father Sanjay Kumar during the students' agitation at Jantar Mantar on June 23 and later recanted fearing legal trouble, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr on Friday. items.headline: Centre to hold fresh Ladakh talks on September 9
items.gist: The Central government will hold a fresh round of talks with Ladakh representatives in New Delhi on September 9, three weeks after the August 19 meeting in Leh ended without a breakthrough on the political framework sought by the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance. Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra confirmed the MHA subcommittee meeting; the groups' "non-negotiable" demands include a directly elected Legislative Assembly headed by a Chief Minister and Council of Ministers, substantial control over finances and law and order, a separate Public Service Commission, and constitutional safeguards drawing on provisions available to states such as Nagaland, Sikkim and Mizoram.

items.headline: Raise judicial officers' retiring age, 7 states told
items.gist: The Supreme Court directed seven consenting states—Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal—to amend service rules and raise judicial officers' retirement age from 60 to 62 years, preferably within two months, subject to high court suitability assessment at age 60. Officers who superannuated on or after March 31 this year may re-join if they have not obtained subsequent employment; the court also asked 24 other states and Union Territories to reconsider enhancing retirement age within two weeks and submit compliance reports.

items.headline: 'Cops assaulting protesters distressing'
items.gist: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said police personnel assaulting protesting students and demonstrators at Jantar Mantar was "distressing" and "a matter of grave concern" while speaking at the launch of "Policing the Republic" by former secretary (security) Yashovardhan Azad in New Delhi. He said it was dismaying to see young IPS officers personally assaulting protesters and warned that the detachment expected of police officers "somehow seems to be disappearing."

items.headline: SC backs NCTE's teacher appraisal directive
items.gist: The Supreme Court upheld an NCTE public notice requiring Teacher Education Institutions to submit annual Performance Appraisal Reports, setting aside a March 2023 Delhi High Court order that had struck down the September 22, 2019 notice as arbitrary. Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe held the NCTE Executive Committee Member Secretary was fully empowered to issue the directive and expanded Article 21A duty bearers to include TEIs and the NCTE as the sixth and seventh responsible parties alongside government, local authorities, schools, parents and teachers.

items.headline: TN woman in Gulf gets Embassy help
items.gist: The Indian Embassy in Kuwait has stepped in to assist Vanitha, a Tamil Nadu domestic worker who appealed in a video for help returning home after being tortured and denied payment for months. items.headline: India, Belgium should work on lab-grown diamonds: Minister
items.gist: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal on Friday suggested India and Belgium collaborate on lab-grown diamonds' technology and certification, speaking at a high-level India-EU FTA dialogue with visiting Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever in Mumbai. items.headline: Keralam BJP picks 'Mission 2029' in-charge for polls
items.gist: Keralam BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar on Friday announced organisational changes for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, appointing general secretary Anoop Antony—close to Prime Minister Narendra Modi—as "Mission 2029" narrative in-charge and state-cell in-charge, dividing 14 districts into two clusters under M T Ramesh and S Suresh, and naming vice-president Shone George in charge of Minority Morcha, state media and social media. Party sources said the focus is bringing more youngsters to leadership roles, and giving key roles to Anoop Antony and Shone George is seen as wooing the Christian community after their strong Assembly poll performances in Christian belts.

items.headline: Keralam Imam counters 'anti-women' remark
items.gist: Palayam mosque Imam V P Suhaib Moulavi countered Grand Mufti of India A P Aboobacker Musliyar's remark that bringing women onto public platforms could lead to "great destruction," stating in his Friday sermon that Islam has no gender discrimination and encourages women's social participation. items.headline: CPI(ML)L to launch campaign against Centre
items.gist: The CPI(ML) Liberation is launching a "School Theek Karo-Sikhsha Sudharo" campaign from Sunday, capitalising on "Gen Z anger" against the Modi government, with at least eight programmes planned in Uttar Pradesh this month. Party general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya and AISA president Neha Bora—who sat on an indefinite hunger strike in July—will participate in a Patna programme on Sunday, with the phase expected to culminate on October 5 at Kolkata's Jadavpur University; the party has already held related programmes in Keralam, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Telangana and Maharashtra.

items.headline: Bombay HC slams Maha over manual scavenging
items.gist: The Bombay High Court quashed a Maharashtra government policy shifting compensation for sewer deaths onto private societies and employers, directing the state to immediately pay Rs 30,00,000 to dependants of each person who died in hazardous cleaning and recover amounts from responsible private entities later. Justices Bharati Dangre and Manjusha Deshpande, ruling on a Shramik Janata Sangh petition against December 12, 2019 and April 30, 2025 government resolutions, ordered identification within six months of all such deaths under the 2013 Manual Scavengers Act and lamented that caste-driven manual scavenging persists despite India reaching the moon.

items.gist: Security forces killed an unidentified terrorist in Budgam's Ashdar Gali on Friday during Operation 'Ashdar', the second confirmed gunfight in the Kashmir Valley this year, after acting on intelligence about insurgent movement from Pakherpora in Pulwama towards Yousmarg. The Army's Chinar Corps said troops observed suspicious activity, were fired upon when challenged, and recovered one AK rifle and war-like stores; the operation in the rugged Pir Panjal terrain follows a relative lull since Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Zakir Ahmad Ganie was killed in Shopian in July.

items.headline: Court allows couple in 50s to pursue IVF after son's death
items.gist: The Gujarat High Court on September 2 allowed a couple in their 50s to access IVF after a doctor refused treatment citing age limits, permitting them to avail Assisted Reproductive Technology services. The couple, whose 25-year-old son died by suicide in 2022 while pursuing medical studies, had two children and sought another child after the mother attained menopause and could not conceive naturally; Justice Nirzar Desai allowed their petition.

items.gist: Journalists Shaheen Khan and Nafeesa Khan said on Friday they would move the Delhi High Court to demand CCTV footage of an alleged assault at a south Delhi police station, making the demand at a press conference with their digital news channel editor Sanjay Sharma, who also plans to approach the court. Police rejected the allegations, saying the two women obstructed a designated VVIP route by parking their scooter and refused repeated requests to comply.

items.headline: RBI absorbs Rs 6.02 L cr; banking system liquidity surplus hits high
items.gist: The Reserve Bank of India on Friday absorbed over Rs 6.02 lakh crore from the banking system through two variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auctions as surplus liquidity remained at a record high. The central bank accepted bids worth Rs 5,41,975 crore in a three-day VRRR auction against a notified Rs 7 lakh crore at a cut-off rate of 5.24 per cent, and Rs 60,419 crore in another three-day auction against Rs 1.5 lakh crore, also at 5.24 per cent.

Liquidity surplus is estimated at around Rs 10.32 lakh crore as on September 3, following large inflows through the special FCNR(B) deposit scheme that mobilised USD 136.38 billion by August 31.

items.headline: Fin Min notifies norms allowing e-commerce firms to maintain inventory only for exports
items.gist: The Department of Economic Affairs has notified changes in Foreign Direct Investment norms to allow e-commerce firms to maintain inventory exclusively for export purposes, requiring them to export goods manufactured or produced in India under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 and related regulations. The September 2 notification adds the provision to the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019, bringing into force a decision announced in July; FDI in inventory-based e-commerce retailing for domestic sales remains not permitted.

items.headline: NSE gets SEBI nod for ₹30,000-crore IPO
items.gist: The National Stock Exchange of India has received SEBI's letter of observation clearing its Draft Red Herring Prospectus for a ₹30,000-crore initial public offering, potentially making it India's second-largest IPO after the proposed Jio Platforms listing. NSE filed the DRHP on June 17 after nearly a decade of delay; the offer will be entirely an offer for sale of up to 14.89 crore equity shares, about 6% of paid-up capital, with no fresh issue.

items.headline: Adobe names Anil Chakravarthy as new president and CEO
items.gist: Adobe on Thursday named Anil Chakravarthy, president of its Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations, as President and CEO effective December 1, succeeding Shantanu Narayen who transitions to Executive Chair after more than 18 years. An IIT (BHU) Varanasi and MIT alumnus who studied in Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, during 1983–85 and previously served four years as Informatica's CEO, Chakravarthy was chosen as David Wadhwani, president of Adobe's Creativity and Productivity Business, announced his departure.

items.headline: Forex kitty jumps to all-time high of $740.8 bn
items.gist: India's forex reserves jumped USD 11.475 billion to a new all-time high of USD 740.803 billion during the week ended August 28, the RBI said on Friday, up from USD 729.328 billion the previous week. The prior record of USD 728.494 billion was set in the week ended February 27, before Middle East conflict led to weeks of decline as the RBI intervened through dollar sales; reserves have since risen after concessional forex swap initiatives announced in June amid rupee depreciation, yielding over USD 132 billion in new flows.

items.headline: Chasing the ghost of the HIMALAYAS
items.gist: Conservationist Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi, who has tracked snow leopards in high-altitude plateaus for two decades, recounts spotting his first wild snow leopard in Spiti Valley on January 27, 2007, and later leading the women-led Shen handicraft enterprise and India Programme of the Snow Leopard Trust. He warns that downgrading the IUCN status without adequate data, solar parks fragmenting habitat, and compensation-only approaches ignore villagers' emotional ties to livestock; his book 'The Ghost of the Mountains' is out now from Penguin Random House.

He warns that downgrading the IUCN status without adequate data, solar parks fragmenting habitat, and compensation-only approaches ignore villagers' emotional ties to livestock; his book 'The Ghost of the Mountains' is out now from Penguin Random House. India is estimated to have about 700 snow leopards, with roughly two-thirds in Ladakh, while the global population is put at 3,500 to 7,000.

items.headline: Mirzapur: The Movie — Cult franchise, enjoyable on big screen
items.gist: The theatrical 'Mirzapur' film, directed by Gurmeet Singh, brings Kaleen Bhaiyya (Pankaj Tripathi), Guddu (Ali Fazal), Bablu (Jitendra Kumar) and rival drug lord Babban Yadav (Ravi Kishan) to the big screen with taut direction, whip-smart dialogues and gory violence. As Babban closes in on Kaleen in the second half, loyalty is tested in a blood-curdling climax; Pankaj Tripathi, Ravi Kishan, Jitendra Kumar, Divyendu Sharma and Sheeba Chadda deliver outstanding performances.

items.headline: Delhi cops allegedly assault 2 Muslim journos
items.gist: Two women journalists, Shaheen and Nafisa Khan, were allegedly detained and assaulted by Delhi Police on Thursday while covering a private hospital event attended by Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta; Shaheen alleged they were beaten with batons for posing questions and because they are Muslims. items.headline: 'Hatemonger' who bragged about cracking man's skull detained after CJP protest
items.gist: Delhi Police detained Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj in Uttar Pradesh on Friday, hours after the Cockroach Janta Party protested outside Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest for assaulting Dalit victim Sanjay Kumar's father — a crime Bhardwaj bragged about in an interview, claiming he cracked the skull, the man needed 60 stitches, and he was not jailed due to political connections. CJP representatives with Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad and MP Pappu Yadav were assured action within 72 hours and sought attempt-to-murder, criminal intimidation and SC/ST Act charges plus a separate FIR over alleged rape threats and abuse targeting Kumar's daughter Nishu.

items.headline: BEML, UMPESL forge partnership to drive next-generation mining fleet productivity
items.gist: Leading defence PSU BEML has signed a strategic MoU with Universal MEP Projects and Engineering Services Limited (UMPESL), a wholly owned Voltas subsidiary, to jointly pursue productivity-driven Fleet Management Contracts across India's coal-fields. Signed at BEML Headquarters in Bengaluru, the partnership combines BEML's OEM expertise in heavy mining equipment with UMPESL's field service and fleet management capabilities, focusing on O&M projects for Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries covering bulldozers, excavators, loaders, dumpers and surface miners.

items.headline: How is demand for good schools anti-govt narrative, asks Dipke
items.gist: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has asked how a demand for good schools or improvement in their condition can be termed an anti-government narrative, urging Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to visit 'ashramshalas' for a "reality check" after meeting tribal students protesting in Nashik. More than 100 tribal students from different parts of Maharashtra are participating in the protest at Eidgah ground in Nashik, with three on hunger strike over demands including better food and students' safety; Dipke said the disparity in facilities, food and education provided to tribal students was "completely unacceptable" and criticised what he called the government's policy of privatising schools and educational facilities.

items.headline: Naidu asks TDP cadre to gear up for local body polls
items.gist: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Thursday directed the TDP machinery to gear up for the upcoming local body elections and aim for a better strike rate than in the 2024 Assembly polls, while stressing coordination among NDA partners. At a meeting with ministers and zonal observers, Naidu said the local body elections would provide an opportunity to assess the party's current position compared to the 2024 polls and noted this would be the first time the TDP would face local elections as part of an alliance, adding that there should be no gap between alliance parties under any circumstances.

items.headline: Release Nagarjuna Sagar water, warns KTR
items.gist: BRS Working President K T Rama Rao said he would undertake a padayatra from Kodad to Haliya with thousands of farmers if the Telangana government failed to announce a schedule for releasing water into the Nagarjuna Sagar Left Canal by September 14. Alleging that the Congress government was withholding water from the Left Canal despite around 180 TMC being available in the Nagarjuna Sagar project, KTR said farmers were anxious about their crops and demanded a clear water-release schedule by September 14.

items.headline: Temples of Goa were destroyed by Portuguese: CM
items.gist: Goa would have had temples comparable to those in south India had the Portuguese not arrived in the coastal state, Chief Minister Pramod Sawant said on Friday while announcing the restoration of the historic Koti Tirth site in Divar. Sawant said several temples were destroyed during Portuguese rule and the Koti Tirth Corridor project, envisioned as a heritage initiative representing temples and religious sites destroyed during the Portuguese period, would be completed within a year; he also said the ancient Gopakapattana Port in St Andre constituency would be developed in the future.

items.headline: 37 evacuated as bus catches fire
items.gist: All 37 people aboard a Bengaluru-Hyderabad private bus escaped unhurt after it caught fire near Miduturu village in Anantapur district in the early hours of Friday, police said. The fire broke out at around 2.50 am at the rear of the vehicle due to unknown causes; a passenger seated at the back spotted the flames and alerted the driver, who stopped the bus immediately, allowing all 33 passengers and four staff members to get off safely before the fire engulfed the vehicle.

items.headline: Maha govt must frame policy on loud DJs: Raut
items.gist: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Friday said the Maharashtra government must formulate a policy on the use of high-decibel DJ sound systems and laser lights during festivals, alleging that Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis lacks the courage to act on the issue. Criticising the state government following the attack on activist Vidyanand Bapat, who was assaulted on Thursday in Pune while campaigning against noise pollution during Ganeshotsav, Raut said isolated bans in cities were inadequate as the issue concerns public health; the Nagpur police on Thursday issued an order banning high-powered and modified sound systems as well as beams and laser lights during the forthcoming festival season.

items.headline: 9 newborns evacuated as fire erupts in NICU of private hospital
items.gist: Nine newborns were shifted after a fire broke out in the NICU of Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, in the early hours of Friday, the hospital administration said. Dr Shoeb Hashmi said staff noticed smoke coming out of an AC unit in the NICU and, as a precaution, the team evacuated the infants along with patients in the neighbouring general ward; the newborns were shifted to other hospitals with family consent, no injuries were reported, and the hospital has been cleaned and is functioning as per routine.

items.headline: Bandi Sanjay slams Telangana CM over 'patriotism' remarks on Owaisi brothers
items.gist: Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar on Friday hit out at Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy over his remarks that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi and his brother Akbaruddin Owaisi were as patriotic as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Bandi Sanjay questioned whether AIMIM's alleged opposition to the full version of Vande Mataram, the abrogation of Article 370 and the Citizenship Amendment Act amounted to patriotism, cited a controversial 2013 speech by Akbaruddin Owaisi and alleged terror links involving institutions connected to the Owaisi family, asking whether the CM should first clarify to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, who had accused AIMIM of helping the BJP, before issuing "certificates" of patriotism.

items.headline: Brahmin activist ends hunger strike
items.gist: Brahmin community activist Deepak Rannaware ended his hunger strike in Jalna on Friday following the intervention of state BJP spokesperson Ram Kulkarni. Rannaware had been on a hunger strike at Gandhi Chaman for the past six days seeking resolution of various demands concerning the Brahmin community; Kulkarni visited the protest site, apprised Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Jalna district guardian minister Pankaja Munde about the demands, and it was decided that a meeting between representatives of the Brahmin community and Fadnavis would be held in Mumbai soon.

items.headline: How India shaped the feminist vision of Gloria Steinem
items.gist: The passing of renowned American feminist pioneer Gloria Steinem on Thursday at the age of 92 has triggered tributes highlighting the deep, lifelong connection she maintained with India. A 22-year-old Steinem arrived in India in 1956 on a Chester Bowles Asian Fellowship, spending nearly two years in the country including about a year at Miranda House hostel in Delhi, travelling alone in third-class women-only railway carriages, walking with Gandhian activists in Ramnad, Tamil Nadu, and participating in Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan land-reform movement; the collective listening practice of village meetings under kerosene lamps became her most enduring organizational tool, later translated into the consciousness-raising groups that drove the American women's movement, and she formed lifelong bonds with Indian feminists including Devaki Jain, Ela Bhatt, Ruchira Gupta and Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay.

items.headline: Needle found in baby's body; medical neglect alleged
items.gist: A needle was found lodged inside a one-year-old girl's body, with her parents alleging on Friday that it may have been left behind during treatment at Kottayam Medical College Hospital. The needle was detected near the child's right ribs during examination at Kozhikode Medical College Hospital in July 2026 and surgically removed; the child, daughter of Anju and Vineesh of Chathamangalam in Kozhikode district, was born at Kottayam Medical College Hospital in June 2025 and shifted to the NICU after developing jaundice, and Anju said doctors dismissed a swelling near her right ribs as a minor growth that would subside, until scans at Kozhikode Medical College Hospital in July 2026 revealed the needle, which doctors said appeared to have been inside the body for a considerable period.

items.headline: TN woman in Kuwait alleges abuse
items.gist: A domestic worker from Kallakurichi district has sent an SOS video from Kuwait, alleging torture, starvation and non-payment of wages by her employers and appealing to Indian authorities to rescue her. The woman, who said she travelled to Kuwait three months ago through an employment agent, alleged she had been denied proper food for more than 50 days and not paid her salary for the past two months, requesting Collector J E Padmaja and SP Shahnaz I to rescue her alive; her mother Vennila appealed to the district administration, alleging an employment agent had misled the family about job conditions.

items.headline: Indigo plane hits pole at Srinagar airport
items.gist: An IndiGo flight operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar collided with a parking stand pole during the parking process at Srinagar International Airport on Friday. Flight 6E 225 came into contact with a metal pole while being positioned at Bay No.
items.paragraph: An IndiGo flight operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar collided with a parking stand pole during the parking process at Srinagar International Airport on Friday. Flight 6E 225 came into contact with a metal pole while being positioned at Bay No. 6 shortly after landing; all passengers and crew remained safe with no injuries reported, everyone deplaned using manual aircraft stairs, and the aircraft has been grounded for necessary maintenance while an investigation is underway.

items.headline: End attacks on TMC, Mamata warns BJP
items.gist: TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee on Thursday turned the alleged attack on her party's Camac Street office into a direct political challenge to the ruling BJP, warning that she would travel to New Delhi and stage dharnas outside the residences of its leaders if "atrocities" against the Trinamool continued. In a combative Facebook Live, Banerjee accused the BJP of sending "goons" to vandalise the TMC office in the early hours, assault party workers and loot documents and electronic equipment; TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged armed men backed by the BJP stormed the office around 4.30 am, and police have arrested six people in connection with the incident.

items.headline: SC dismisses NEET-PG 2026 re-test plea
items.gist: The Supreme Court has dismissed a Public Interest Litigation seeking a fresh conduct of the NEET-PG 2026 examination, severely admonishing the petitioner and counsel for misusing judicial forums and creating nationwide panic. A bench comprising Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe threw out the petition, levying a penalty of ₹25,000 on the petitioner and warning it would refer the petitioner's advocate to the Bar Council of India for disciplinary action regarding social media solicitation; NBEMS clarified that out of 1,111 centres across India, administrative power outages were limited to only two centres at the iON Digital Zone in Jaipur affecting around 2,500 candidates, and the petitioners from Noida and Punjab were entirely unaffected and not even appearing in the exam themselves.

items.headline: Row over women's role: Islamic scholar urges followers not to be 'provoked'
items.gist: Islamic scholar Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar, facing criticism over his alleged anti-women remarks, on Friday urged his followers not to be provoked or allow "spiritual discussions" to be diverted into controversies and divisions. In a Facebook post, the veteran Sunni scholar said discussions should provide healthy platforms to objectively assess ideas and learn new things, alleged that vested interests deliberately try to divert spiritual discussions towards controversies and divisions, and urged followers to respond to any provocation with maturity and wisdom rather than emotion, noting that the tradition of Sunni believers has always been to confront all evils only with goodness.

items.headline: El Nino to get worse; what it means for India
items.gist: The prevailing El Nino conditions over the equatorial Pacific are most likely to intensify into a very strong event in the coming months and persist through February 2027, the World Meteorological Organization has said, warning of substantial impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat. The IMD confirmed that overall rainfall in India during August was deficient at 16 per cent due to prevailing El Nino conditions, with August being the hottest since 1901, and has forecast September rainfall to be below 91 per cent of the long period average; an intensifying El Nino means higher temperatures during the winter season, with a Climate Trends study finding February-March warming in northern India is increasing the risk of terminal heat stress on Rabi crops like wheat during reproductive and grain filling stages.

items.headline: Ola Electric's first dealer stores are now open across India
items.gist: Ola Electric on Friday launched its first cohort of network-partner stores, with dealer-operated outlets going live in Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Bihar, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. The stores deepen the company's regional presence and will serve local demand for Ola scooters and motorcycles, marking a structural shift five years after Ola opened its first scooter through a fully company-owned model.

items.headline: Sensex rebounds 362 pts, snaps 4-day losses
items.gist: Benchmark BSE Sensex rebounded 362.57 points, or 0.48 per cent, to settle at 76,515.43 on Friday, snapping a four-day losing streak on buying in metal, private banking and oil and gas shares amid gains in global stock markets, with 20 of 30 constituents ending higher. The barometer surged as much as 730.28 points intra-day to 76,883.14, while the NSE Nifty rose a modest 24.25 points, or 0.10 per cent, to 23,897.70 after paring gains in the Closing Auction Session despite briefly breaching 24,000.

items.headline: Panel meet fails to arrive at consensus on water sharing
items.gist: A three-member Krishna River Management Board committee meeting in Hyderabad on Friday failed to agree on the water-sharing proportion for 2026-27 amid El Nino conditions, as Andhra Pradesh insisted on continuing the ad hoc 66:34 (AP:TG) arrangement agreed for 2015-16 while Telangana stood firm for a 50% share since 2020. After deadlock in two successive meetings, another session was scheduled for the fourth week of September, and officials said a full-fledged meeting with State Secretaries and the board Chairman is likely in the last week of this month; as on September 4, Srisailam had received 213.6 tmc ft inflows since June 1 while Nagarjunasagar received 93.1 tmc ft including releases from Srisailam.

items.headline: Don't attack crocodiles, forest staff tell public after viral clip
items.gist: Forest Department officials in Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, have warned the public not to harm crocodiles after a viral video showed people trying to beat a crocodile with sticks on the banks of the Tungabhadra at Naguladinne village. The Kurnool District Forest Officer said crocodiles are protected under Schedule-1 of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and officials noted crocodiles are coming out of rivers as water levels have reduced.

items.headline: Keralam govt. finalises terms of reference for Messi visit SIT probe
items.gist: The Congress-led United Democratic Front government has fixed the terms of reference for an SIT probe into allegations of service tax fraud, corruption, suspected money-laundering, abuse of constitutional office and nepotism surrounding the previous LDF government's failed attempt to bring the Argentina football team and Lionel Messi for a friendly at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Kochi in August 2025. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has signed off on a remit covering the entire transaction from its inception in 2024, including sponsor selection and information on a U.S.-based entity that allegedly wire-transferred ₹126 crore to the Argentina Football Association in 2025, triggering an unredeemed service tax obligation of ₹22.68 crore to the State exchequer.

items.headline: Missing: boundary walls, bathrooms, blackboards
items.gist: Since August 15, Abhijeet Dipke's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) "School thik karo (reform schools)" campaign has spotlighted rural government schools through a three-step public audit—download a checklist, conduct the audit, and submit and tag the CJP—covering drinking water, boundary walls, washrooms, and midday meals. In Bihar, Muzaffarpur's Dumri Kewat Tola primary school (119 students, established 1982) has no boundary wall, washroom, sports ground, or midday-meal storage, with children relieving themselves in the open, while nearby Budhnagra middle school crams 283 students into two rooms and Vaishali's Mirpur Pathad school runs 91 students in a single community-centre room; in Rajasthan's Deeg district, students at Rajkiya Prathmik Vidyalayas in Unchki, Amrooka, and Bas Bolkheda walk through graveyards or muddy paths, study in corridors, lack toilets, and see only 50–60% daily attendance.

items.headline: CBI searches 89 locations across 20 States in crackdown against 3 'digital arrest' cases
items.gist: The CBI carried out searches at 89 locations across 20 States in three major "digital arrest" scam cases under Operation Chakra-VI, arresting three persons and seizing banking documents, digital devices and other evidence. In one case linked to BITS Pilani, a victim was kept under "digital arrest" for three months and extorted of ₹7.67 crore; in Gujarat, a victim lost ₹19.24 crore over three months; and in Karnataka, a victim paid ₹15.45 crore over one month.

items.headline: Air India sacks Delhi-Phuket flight pilot after AAIB report
items.gist: Air India on Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of an Aug. 4 Delhi-Phuket flight after he tested positive for psychoactive substance in a confirmatory test; the flight momentarily lost altitude, injuring 24 passengers.
items.paragraph: Air India on Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of an Aug. 4 Delhi-Phuket flight after he tested positive for psychoactive substance in a confirmatory test; the flight momentarily lost altitude, injuring 24 passengers. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report recommended DGCA action on priority, noting all three hydraulic systems failed, the autopilot disengaged and a stall warning sounded for two seconds as the aircraft gained 372 ft and fell 292 ft from flight level 360; a detailed probe into technical aspects is under way. The co-pilot regained control as systems recovered, but with seatbelt signs off at cruising altitude, passengers and crew were injured and the cabin sustained damage including cracked ceiling panels, broken handrails and a dislodged lavatory commode.

items.headline: NCPCR campaign rescues over 3,800 from child labour
items.gist: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights has rescued over 3,800 children from child labour and registered more than 575 FIRs under a Pan-India Rescue and Rehabilitation campaign launched on June 12 and run until August 31. The statutory body coordinated with State and UT administrations, district magistrates, labour departments and police to identify, rescue and rehabilitate children in labour and those vulnerable to trafficking, and held district-level meetings to review operations and strengthen inter-department coordination.

items.headline: Centre's rationale for not using OBC lists for caste enumeration is flawed, say associations
items.gist: OBC associations said on Friday that the government's argument that OBC lists cannot be used for caste enumeration because they list "classes, not castes" is "fundamentally flawed," a day after The Hindu reported this as part of the Union rationale for not drawing caste names from Central and State OBC lists for the 2027 Census. The All India OBC Students' Association, OBC Public Representatives Forum chair V.
items.paragraph: OBC associations said on Friday that the government's argument that OBC lists cannot be used for caste enumeration because they list "classes, not castes" is "fundamentally flawed," a day after The Hindu reported this as part of the Union rationale for not drawing caste names from Central and State OBC lists for the 2027 Census. The All India OBC Students' Association, OBC Public Representatives Forum chair V. Srinivas Goud and Backwards Classes Intellectual Forum chairman T. Chiranjeevulu argued the government should rationalise caste names from existing lists rather than drop them, and that refusing to enumerate OBC populations scientifically could expose overestimation of the EWS-eligible population cited when EWS reservations were introduced; Opposition leaders including Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have questioned relying on an open-column methodology instead.

items.headline: Two held for sexual abuse of students in Bihar school
items.gist: Bihar Police arrested headmaster Mohammad Imam Ali Ansari and teacher Arvind Kumar of a government school in Dumraon over alleged sexual abuse of schoolgirls; teacher Virendra Prasad remains absconding. The accused are charged with sexually abusing the girls, circulating objectionable videos and threatening them through audio messages under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act, following a complaint by a student's mother.

items.headline: Emergency broadcasting of weather and natural disaster alerts resumed: C-DOT CEO
items.gist: C-DOT CEO Rajkumar Upadhyay told The Hindu that the emergency cell broadcasting service for extreme weather and natural disasters has "already resumed" after a brief suspension following an erroneous late-night alert in central Delhi. Developed by C-DOT and operated by State Disaster Management Agencies, the system required 300–350 adapters to reach diverse telecom equipment; Utimaco had sued the government over handing the project to C-DOT, and the Delhi High Court ruled in the government's favour while allowing the firm to pursue damages.

items.headline: Violence breaks out in Arunachal over inclusions in SIR
items.gist: Alleged inclusion of Chakma and Hajong community members in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls sparked violence in Bordumsa, Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh, on Friday, with firing and stone-pelting leaving at least one person injured, reportedly an All Arunachal Pradesh Students' Union member. The Buddhist Chakmas and Hindu Hajongs, displaced from erstwhile East Pakistan's Chittagong Hill Tracts and settled by the Centre in the 1960s, are opposed by AAPSU and local groups over inclusion of non-indigenous communities, especially those allegedly settled after 2006; AAPSU president Meje Taku demanded suspension of SIR in Chakma and Hajong areas, arrest of those who targeted protest leaders, and that no FIR be registered against AAPSU members.

items.headline: Belgian port can be key to Indian exports: De Wever
items.gist: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever, in Mumbai on Friday for a high-level dialogue on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, pitched the Port of Antwerp-Bruges as a gateway for Indian exports to Europe in sectors including diamonds, pharmaceuticals, food processing, maritime services, green hydrogen and infrastructure. Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal invited Belgian companies to invest in India and said the FTA, under discussion for around 25 years and covering about two billion people and roughly $24 trillion in market value, would eliminate or reduce tariffs on more than 95% of Indian and European goods exports; bilateral trade stood at approximately $13.08 billion in 2025-26, with India-Belgium gems and jewellery trade at around $3.5 billion.

items.headline: On Nepal Minister seeking damages, India says climate change a common challenge
items.gist: External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Friday that climate change is a "common challenge" and developed nations that are "historically" the highest emitters must lead in reducing emissions and supporting developing countries through finance and technology transfer. The remarks responded to Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who had said the U.S., China and India—as the three biggest greenhouse gas emitters—should bear responsibility for climate change and sought compensation after the August 26 flash flood; Khanal later denied seeking compensation and expressed "deep gratitude" for Indian help, while Jaiswal noted India has sent relief including tunnel rescue specialists and that Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah thanked India in Parliament.

items.headline: Congress stands with 'all daughters' fighting for justice, says leader Alka Lamba
items.gist: All India Mahila Congress president Alka Lamba said on Friday that the Congress stands with "all the daughters" fighting for justice and will extend every possible support to them, citing the alleged assault of student activist Nishu Azad's father at a Jantar Mantar protest and cases involving journalists Shaheen Khan and Nafisa Khan and student activist Akriti Chaudhary, who was arrested under the National Security Act in Noida before the Allahabad High Court revoked it. She demanded action including provisions relating to attempted murder against self-styled "Hindutva influencer" Swatantra Bhardwaj, accused in the Azad matter, and called for suspension of Delhi Police personnel and release of CCTV footage after the journalists alleged they were detained and beaten while covering an event attended by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

items.headline: CPI(ML) to seek reforms in education in Bihar, U.P.
items.gist: The CPI (ML) Liberation is set to launch a one-month campaign seeking reforms in the education sector, beginning in Patna with a public meeting on September 6, highlighting inadequate school and college infrastructure and concerns over National Education Policy implementation. Primarily focused on Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, party campaigners will travel extensively across the region to establish contact with young voters ahead of Assembly elections scheduled for early next year.

items.headline: 275 Indians still missing, 169 rescued, says Ministry
items.gist: The Kailash Manasarovar Yatra of 2026 has ended officially as all Indian pilgrims have left Chinese territory bordering Nepal following the August 26 flash flood in the Bhote Koshi river, the External Affairs Ministry said on Friday. Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that 275 Indian nationals remain missing and 169 Indians have been rescued, with numbers possibly fluctuating as survivors are still being discovered; apart from government-assisted tours, private travellers used the Nepali route through the Gyirong border crossing, where a significant number went missing when the port was hit by the flash flood.

items.headline: Army kills one terrorist in forest area of J&K's Budgam
items.gist: One terrorist was killed on Friday during a joint operation by the Army and Jammu and Kashmir Police deep inside a forest area in Budgam district, officials said. The operation was launched based on information about the movement of a suspected group of terrorists from Pulwama district towards Budgam; based on specific intelligence input, the Indian Army, J&K Police and CRPF launched a joint search in Ashdar Gali, Budgam, and the operation is under way as forces are still looking for another terrorist believed to be holed up in the same area.

items.headline: 82 educators set to receive National Teachers' Awards
items.gist: An asteroid hunter, a Maths wizard, a trailblazer in a coal mining community and a Special Olympics hockey coach are among 82 educators from across the country who will receive the National Teachers' Awards on Saturday, to be conferred by President Droupadi Murmu. Among the awardees are 48 school teachers, 21 faculty members in higher education, and 13 trainers from the Union Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; notable recipients include Haryana-based Anil Kaushik, the 'Math Wizard'; Rajasthan-based Divyendu Sen, who trained students to track asteroids; Jaipur teacher Vartika Gulati; and Odisha-based Padaraj Nayak, whose students built a low-cost automatic plate-washing machine that earned a Government of India patent.

items.headline: SC pushes for raising retirement age in district judiciary as backlog tops 5 cr.
items.gist: As 5.18 crore cases lie pending in district courts across the country, the Supreme Court has sent a distress call to States to enhance the retirement age of experienced judicial officers from 60 to 62 years, calling it the "crying need of the hour" to stop attrition of experienced judicial talent lest access to justice remain a mere chimera due to unfilled posts. Only seven States — Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal — have responded positively; a three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant directed them to amend service rules within two months and gave hesitant States, including Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Kerala, Punjab, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and others, two weeks to decide on enhancement to 62 years.

items.headline: Over 17,000 shifted to safer places amid floods in U.P.
items.gist: More than 17,500 people have been evacuated from 26 flood-affected districts across Uttar Pradesh, with no loss of life or livestock reported so far, the State government said on Friday. Eight rivers are flowing above the danger mark; around 3.53 lakh people have been affected, while 4,847 people are currently staying in relief shelters.

The Relief Commissioner's office said 72,897 flood relief kits and more than 3.67 lakh lunch packets have been distributed, along with more than 5.52 lakh chlorine tablets and over 1.87 lakh ORS packets for health safety.

items.headline: NTA seeks AICTE help to establish centres for computer-based tests
items.gist: The National Testing Agency has sought the help of the All India Council for Technical Education to map IT infrastructure and vacant spaces in government institutions to establish standard testing centres for computer-based testing for NTA examinations, including NEET. The NTA plans to shift NEET to CBT mode next year; nearly 22 lakh students appeared for NEET-UG 2026 in pen-and-paper format, which became embroiled in a paper leak controversy and had to be re-conducted.

items.headline: Thermal sector grapples with coal stock management
items.gist: India's thermal power sector faces a fuel management dilemma in which generators maintaining adequate coal inventories can be disadvantaged when limited domestic supplies are redirected to plants that fall below prescribed stock norms. Industry stakeholders warn that repeated emergency redistribution, while sometimes needed for grid reliability, could undermine incentives to plan inventories under the CEA framework in effect since December 6, 2021 and the revised SHAKTI policy approved in May 2025.
items.paragraph: India's thermal power sector faces a fuel management dilemma in which generators maintaining adequate coal inventories can be disadvantaged when limited domestic supplies are redirected to plants that fall below prescribed stock norms. Industry stakeholders warn that repeated emergency redistribution, while sometimes needed for grid reliability, could undermine incentives to plan inventories under the CEA framework in effect since December 6, 2021 and the revised SHAKTI policy approved in May 2025. National coal production exceeded one billion tonnes in each of the last two financial years and combined stocks at plants, pitheads and in transit stood around 148 MT, indicating the challenge is allocation and logistics rather than an overall shortage.

items.headline: SEBI presses ahead against Hindenburg in Adani case
items.gist: India's markets regulator has started hearing representations as it seeks to recover gains from trades it suspects benefited from prior knowledge of Hindenburg Research's report on Adani Group, more than two years after the episode, according to two people with knowledge of the matter. SEBI believes it has jurisdiction although the parties are overseas because the trades were in India, and is proceeding on the grounds that they violated rules against trading on non-public information.

items.headline: Douglas bullish about India at Asiad
items.gist: Troy Hamilton Douglas, head coach of athletics at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS), Vidhyanagar, Ballari, believes Indian athletics can better its performance at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya after a record 29-medal haul at the Hangzhou Games in 2023 — six gold, 14 silver and nine bronze, India's best-ever athletics tally at the Asian Games since 1951. Douglas, whose contract with IIS runs until 2028, said he would be very happy if India equalled or won two or three more medals and projected the country could win 32 medals after observing Indian athletics for more than a year and watching the Indian Series this season.

items.headline: Records galore on last day of Natl. youth athletics
items.gist: Several meet and national records tumbled on the final day of the 21st National youth athletics championships in Ludhiana on Thursday. Madhya Pradesh's Krishan Chandra won the boys' javelin with 79.92m, bettering the previous meet record of 77.41m set by Rohit Yadav in 2018 in Vadodara, while West Bengal's Misti Karmakar won the girls' javelin gold with 52.84m, surpassing the 51.84m set by Deepika in 2022.

Yash Mulik and Nupura Holla were declared the best male and female athletes respectively; Yash set a national record in the 110m hurdles with 13.40s. Haryana topped the medal tally with four gold, seven silver and three bronze; Maharashtra finished second with eight medals including three gold, and Karnataka finished third with three gold and two silver.

items.headline: Urine causes melting of Everest Base Camp: Study
items.gist: A new study estimates about 3 million kilograms of glacial ice and snow are lost each spring at Everest Base Camp from energy used for climber comforts, with human urine alone responsible for an estimated 154 tons of melt on the Khumbu Glacier. In 2023, researchers recorded 824 cylinders of liquefied petroleum gas, 18,935 litres of kerosene and 5,130 litres of gasoline used for cooking, heating and powering about 1,600 tents, while more than 6,000 litres of urine are produced daily by climbers and guides, most of it deposited directly on the glacier rather than in pit-vault toilets.

items.headline: Pakistan rejects allegations of Hindu temple demolition
items.gist: Pakistan on Friday rejected allegations that a century-old Hindu temple in Siraj village, Narowal, Punjab, was deliberately demolished, asserting torrential rains on July 21 damaged its structure. Local people, minority bodies and a political party had said religious zealots demolished the temple to include its land in an adjacent seminary; India on Wednesday condemned the reported destruction and demanded Islamabad investigate and restore the temple, while Pakistan's Foreign Office called India's allegations "false and politically motivated."

items.headline: Meloni celebrates govt record
items.gist: Giorgia Meloni on Friday celebrated her hard-right government becoming Italy's longest-lasting in the postwar republic, with a rally in Bari expected to draw thousands while protesters demonstrated nearby. Meloni, who became Italy's first woman PM on October 22, 2022, wrote on X that stability "is not a record to be displayed, but the condition that allows a nation to plan, decide, keep its commitments, and be respected."

items.headline: India-born man on FBI list
items.gist: The FBI added India-born Manjit Singh Bedi, a naturalised US citizen, to its most-wanted fraudsters list for allegedly defrauding the US government of at least USD 6 lakh between March 2024 and June 2025 through his Tacoma, Washington grocery store. items.headline: Two workers rescued from tunnel in Nepal 9 days after flash floods
items.gist: Two men—Kabir Maharjan, 45, a mechanical supervisor, and Sanjay Sah, 30, a foreman—were rescued alive on Friday from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project tunnel nine days after flash floods tore through central Nepal's Trishuli River corridor. Maharjan was flown to Nepal Army Hospital in critical condition while Sah, who said he chanted the Hare Krishna mantra for nine days while trapped, is under treatment in Nuwakot; over 1,250 people have died and more than 4,700 remain missing from floods triggered by an August 26 ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border, with over 600 workers at 11 hydropower projects still unaccounted for.
